A1.justification: Both PDFs describe W&C-Sent and contain complete, readable main texts and appendices. Their datasets, experiments, figures, tables, and prompt templates can be matched despite renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original human annotations, agreement and correlation analyses, and model evaluations for 1,633 sentence–target pairs.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and reports additional model evaluations and an analysis of 102 prediction-error instances.

M1.justification: Coarse-grained inference prompts change from label-only JSON output in v1 Appendix O.4–O.5 to an explicit one-sentence reason followed by the label in v2 Appendix N.4–N.5. Fine-grained prompts already requested reasons. The annotation framework, BERTweet architecture, and training losses remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 1,633 English sentence–target pairs drawn from SemEval-2016 and ABCDE, covering seven targets and three social-perception dimensions. The expanded prompt demonstrations do not introduce a new benchmark or evaluation domain.

E2.justification: v2 adds GPT-5.2 Chat and Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 to the zero-shot and few-shot comparisons in both classification settings. The original comparators remain; Gemma/Gemma3, Qwen/Qwen2.5, and BERT/BERTweet naming changes do not represent additional methods.

E3.justification: Fine-grained few-shot prompts expand from five demonstrations to nine for trust, eight for sociability, and nine for competence, covering all labels and revising several examples. The reported annotator total changes from 215 in v1's limitations and 216 in its demographic table to 210 in v2. Dataset splits, training budgets, and the appendix mean-versus-median experiments are retained; these revisions do not establish that annotation was rerun.

E4.justification: v2 Section 4.2 adds a targeted analysis of 102 GPT-4o and Qwen2.5 cases where few-shot predictions diverge from gold labels and zero-shot outputs. Conversely, v1 Appendix Q and Tables 21–22, analyzing Gemma and Qwen output-label distributions, are removed. Existing aggregation comparisons and annotation-agreement analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both versions retain 1,000 split-half reliability repetitions, random seed 13 in the training settings, and standard deviations for stance-group summaries. Table 5 adds means and changes deviation values, but does not introduce a new uncertainty-reporting practice. Neither version reports repeated-run uncertainty for model performance.

E6.justification: Tables 3–4 and their appendix counterparts add GPT-5.2 and Qwen3 results and replace numerous fine-grained few-shot scores. Under revised prompts, Gemma's competence accuracy changes from 0.16 to 0.35, while GPT-4o's changes from 0.30 to 0.24; these are not same-setting gains or losses. GPT-5.2 zero-shot leads v2's coarse sociability comparison with 0.83 accuracy and 0.74 F1. Table 5 adds means and revises standard deviations, demographic counts change, and the earlier output-frequency results disappear.

T1.justification: The rating scale, coarsening rules, and regression/classification loss specifications are retained. Neither version adds formal propositions, proofs, or substantive mathematical derivations.

C1.justification: Both versions claim the first sentence-level warmth-and-competence dataset and emphasize its benchmarking value and models' difficulty capturing social cues. Although v2 removes 'The First' from the title, the novelty claim remains in its abstract and conclusion.

C2.justification: v2 proposes calibration bias, excessive reliance on surface cues, and misinterpreted figurative language as explanations for few-shot failures. It also argues that newer or larger models need not perform better. The earlier Gemma-versus-Qwen decisiveness interpretation is removed, while the principal cultural and applicability limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 removes v1's preprocessing examples in Table 13 and Appendix P's response-parsing, JSON-repair, and label-normalization details. It supplies expanded prompt templates while retaining training hyperparameters and dataset-access information. These documentation removals do not establish that the underlying processing steps were abandoned.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations for the GPT-5 system card and Qwen3 technical report and expands discussion of the existing Words of Warmth lexicon and its applications. The ABCDE reference's publication update denotes the same cited work, not a new research connection.

P1.justification: v2 edits the title and correspondence line, refines introductory and dataset prose, and reorganizes the results discussion around an explicit few-shot-versus-zero-shot subsection. Appendix lettering changes after removals, but the main narrative structure and much of the text remain intact.

P2.justification: The mean and median distribution plots exchange main-text and appendix roles and receive revised styling and axes. Other agreement plots are restyled, Tables 3–4 gain blue ranking highlights, and Table 11 is transposed and compressed. Removed appendix material takes three tables with it. New rows in v2 Table 19 also contain an extra unlabeled numeric column.

improvement.justification: The additional baselines, fuller demonstration-label coverage, and 102-instance error analysis strengthen evaluation. However, v2 removes useful processing documentation and introduces reporting ambiguities: Table 19 has unlabeled extra values, and the revised demographic table conflicts with retained prose percentages. These gains and losses in validation, reproducibility, and numerical clarity prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
